content:
# Sirach 36 — Disagreement Log

**Chapter:** SIR 036 | **Agents:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA | **Total Disagreements:** 16

---

## Disagreement 1 — v.1: address "O Master" vs. "O Lord"

- **EMET:** "O Master, the God of all"
- **LOGOS:** "O Lord God of all"
- **PNEUMA:** "Lord God of all"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "O Lord, God of all" — δέσποτα can be rendered "Master" or "Lord"; "Lord" is the more consistent rendering for this prayer's liturgical register; EMET's "Master" is accurate but unusual.

---

## Disagreement 2 — v.2: "terror" vs. "dread"

- **EMET:** "cast your terror upon all the nations"
- **LOGOS:** "send your dread upon all the nations"
- **PNEUMA:** "Strike all the nations with terror"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "cast your terror upon all the nations" — EMET; φόβον is "fear/terror"; "dread" (LOGOS) is acceptable but "terror" carries stronger military weight appropriate to this nationalist prayer.

---

## Disagreement 3 — v.4: sanctification/magnification parallel

- **EMET:** "As you have been sanctified in us before them, so be magnified in them before us"
- **LOGOS:** "As you have been shown holy in us before them, so be magnified in them before our eyes"
- **PNEUMA:** "Just as you revealed your holiness among us for all to see, now reveal your greatness among them"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "As you have been shown holy among us before them, so be magnified among them before our eyes" — LOGOS's phrasing preserves the parallelism; PNEUMA loses "magnified" (ἐμεγαλύνθης) which is the key verb.

---

## Disagreement 4 — v.6: "renew signs" vs. "repeat your signs"

- **EMET:** "Renew signs and work further wonders"
- **LOGOS:** "Repeat your signs and work new wonders"
- **PNEUMA:** "Do it again: repeat your signs, work new wonders"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "Renew your signs and work further wonders" — combines EMET and LOGOS; "renew" (ἀνακαίνισον) is more precise than "repeat"; "further" is implied by the context.

---

## Disagreement 5 — v.7: "anger" vs. "wrath"

- **EMET:** "Rouse your anger and pour out wrath"
- **LOGOS:** "Stir up your wrath and pour out fury"
- **PNEUMA:** "Unleash your anger; pour out your fury"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "Rouse your wrath and pour out fury" — "wrath" is more solemn than "anger" for this intensifying parallelism; LOGOS's "fury" for the second term is the best choice.

---

## Disagreement 6 — v.8: "hasten the time" vs. "hasten the end"

- **EMET:** "Hasten the time and remember the oath"
- **LOGOS:** "Hasten the end and remember your sworn oath"
- **PNEUMA:** "Bring the moment forward; honor your oath"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "Hasten the time and remember your sworn oath" — καιρόν refers to "the appointed time/moment," not eschatological "end" (LOGOS oversteps); PNEUMA's "honor your oath" is interpretive.

---

## Disagreement 7 — v.9: "burning wrath" vs. "fiery wrath"

- **EMET:** "Let burning wrath devour the survivor"
- **LOGOS:** "Let fiery wrath consume what remains"
- **PNEUMA:** "Let burning wrath consume whatever is left"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "Let fiery wrath consume the survivor" — "fiery" (LOGOS) is most evocative; "consume" is better than "devour."

---

## Disagreement 8 — v.10: "hostile rulers" vs. "rulers of the enemy"

- **EMET:** "the rulers of the enemy, who say"
- **LOGOS:** "hostile rulers who say"
- **PNEUMA:** "rulers who oppress us"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "hostile rulers" (LOGOS) — more compact; PNEUMA's "who oppress us" interprets the following quote.

---

## Disagreement 9 — v.11: "as from the beginning" vs. "as in former times"

- **EMET:** "as from the beginning"
- **LOGOS:** "as in former times"
- **PNEUMA:** "in the beginning"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "as in the beginning" — ἀρχῆθεν points to the original allotment under Joshua; "former times" is acceptable but vaguer.

---

## Disagreement 10 — v.14: "fill Zion with your majesty" vs. "fill with proclamation of deeds"

- **EMET:** "Fill Zion with your majesty"
- **LOGOS:** "Fill Zion with the proclamation of your deeds"
- **PNEUMA:** "Fill Zion with the news of your deeds"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "Fill Zion with the proclamation of your deeds" (LOGOS) — ἐξήγησιν means "narration/proclamation"; EMET's "majesty" translates a different reading.

---

## Disagreement 11 — v.15: "bear witness to those who were your creatures" vs. "bear witness on behalf of"

- **EMET:** "Bear witness to those who were your creatures from the beginning"
- **LOGOS:** "Bear witness on behalf of those you created at the beginning"
- **PNEUMA:** "Vindicate the people you made from the start"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "Bear witness on behalf of those you created from the beginning" (LOGOS) — the Greek ἐπιμαρτύρησον τοῖς ἐξ ἀρχῆς κτίσμασίν σου means "testify in favor of your original creatures."

---

## Disagreement 12 — v.17: "eternal God" vs. "God of the ages"

- **EMET:** "the God of the ages"
- **LOGOS:** "the eternal God"
- **PNEUMA:** "the Lord God who endures forever"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "the eternal God" — clearer in English than "God of the ages" (EMET), and more concise than PNEUMA's expansion.

---

## Disagreement 13 — v.19: "distinguishes between game meats" vs. "tells the difference between kinds of game"

- **EMET:** "distinguishes between game meats"
- **LOGOS:** "tells the difference between game"
- **PNEUMA:** "knows the difference between meats"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "distinguishes between kinds of game" — combines EMET's specificity (game) with LOGOS's compactness.

---

## Disagreement 14 — v.20: "perverse heart" vs. "dishonest heart"

- **EMET:** "A perverse heart will cause sorrow"
- **LOGOS:** "A devious heart causes grief"
- **PNEUMA:** "A dishonest heart brings grief"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "A perverse heart causes grief" — σκολιὰ καρδία means "crooked/twisted heart"; "perverse" is traditional and precise; "devious" (LOGOS) shifts toward intentional deception.

---

## Disagreement 15 — v.24: "possession" vs. "finest possession"

- **EMET:** "enters upon a possession"
- **LOGOS:** "has his finest possession"
- **PNEUMA:** "has found something precious"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "acquires his finest possession" — the superlative is present in some manuscripts; EMET's "enters upon" is too legalistic; PNEUMA loses the property-acquisition metaphor.

---

## Disagreement 16 — v.26: "well-armed robber" vs. "agile robber"

- **EMET:** "well-armed robber that slinks from city to city"
- **LOGOS:** "agile robber that darts from city to city"
- **PNEUMA:** "bandit who slips from town to town"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "agile robber who slips from city to city" — combines LOGOS's "agile" and PNEUMA's "slips"; "darts" (LOGOS) is too energetic for the connotation of furtiveness.
